summary.en: Serve the most urgent key first and compare unsorted arrays, sorted arrays and heaps.
summary.bn: Priority অনুযায়ী আগে কাজ বেছে নাও এবং তিন ধরনের implementation তুলনা করো।

notes: Programs use C17 with explicit bounds and ownership checks.

examples.title: Keep best jobs at the sorted-array end
examples.explanationHtml: Smaller priorities leave first. Arrival breaks the tie between jobs twenty-two and thirty-three.

examples.title: Search an unsorted array on removal
examples.explanationHtml: A scan finds the best pair on every removal. Swapping the last entry into the gap does not change the tie rule.

examples.title: Maintain a binary min-heap
examples.explanationHtml: Sift-up and sift-down preserve the parent-before-child order. The same jobs leave in the same order.

practice.title: Schedule with a sorted array
practice.statementHtml: Read job count 0..16 and id/priority integer pairs. Smaller priority is more urgent; ties follow arrival order. Print the prompt and Job: id Priority: priority for each job, using sorted insertion.
hints: Store the best key at the final live index.

practice.title: Schedule with an unsorted array
practice.statementHtml: Use the same job input, prompt and output as sorted scheduling, but append without sorting and scan for each best job. Preserve FIFO ties.
hints: Include arrival in every comparison, even after gap filling.

practice.title: Schedule with a heap
practice.statementHtml: Read at most sixteen job id/priority pairs. Print the job prompt, then remove all jobs by increasing priority with FIFO ties. Use a binary min-heap.
hints: The better child fills the downward hole before the last entry is placed.

practice.title: Schedule a max-priority queue with stable ties
practice.statementHtml: Read at most sixteen job id/priority pairs. Here larger priorities are more urgent. Print the job prompt and Job:/Priority: lines in service order, keeping FIFO ties.
hints: Reverse only the priority comparison, not the arrival comparison.

options: The best key under its comparison rule
quiz.explanation: The ADT defines a key ordering.

quiz.prompt: For an unsorted array, which update is O(1) before capacity fills?
quiz.explanation: Appending needs no search or shifts.

quiz.prompt: In the sorted implementation, where is the best job stored?
quiz.explanation: The array is arranged worst-to-best for constant-time removal.

quiz.prompt: What are binary-heap insert and remove-min costs?
quiz.explanation: A value follows at most one tree-height path.

quiz.prompt: Does a binary heap guarantee FIFO ties by itself?
options: No; arrival must be part of the key
quiz.explanation: Heap movements do not inherently preserve insertion order.

quiz.prompt: What key does Dijkstra prioritize in its usual min-queue?
quiz.explanation: The shortest-path algorithm expands the cheapest tentative candidate.

quiz.prompt: Why might a scheduler need aging?
options: To prevent low-priority jobs waiting forever
quiz.explanation: Repeated urgent arrivals can starve other jobs.

quiz.prompt: Which priority wins a min-priority comparison of 2 and 5?
quiz.explanation: Smaller priorities win in this convention.

quiz.prompt: What parent index belongs to heap index six?
quiz.explanation: Zero-based heap parent uses integer division.

quiz.prompt: Which arrival wins a tie between sequence numbers three and seven?
quiz.explanation: The earlier sequence number wins equal-priority comparisons.

quiz.prompt: Which sequence of heap array priorities can satisfy min-heap order without being sorted?
quiz.explanation: One is no greater than either child; the two children need not be ordered.

quiz.prompt: Why does better compare priorities without subtracting them?
options: Subtraction can overflow for extreme int keys
quiz.explanation: Relational comparison avoids computing a possibly out-of-range difference.

keyPoints.en: A priority queue removes the best key rather than the oldest arrival.
keyPoints.bn: Priority queue-তে সবচেয়ে জরুরি key আগে বের হয়।

keyPoints.en: This min-priority convention treats smaller numbers as more urgent.
keyPoints.bn: এখানে ছোট priority সংখ্যা বেশি জরুরি বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: Arrival order breaks equal-priority ties explicitly.
keyPoints.bn: Priority সমান হলে আসার ক্রম আলাদা করে তুলনা করো।

keyPoints.en: A heap orders parents against children without sorting every pair.
keyPoints.bn: Heap-এ parent ও child-এর নিয়ম থাকে, সব মান সাজানো থাকে না।

keyPoints.en: Scheduling and shortest-path exploration use different priority policies.
keyPoints.bn: Scheduling আর shortest path-এ priority-এর অর্থ আলাদা।

examQuestions.question: Schedule jobs (id 5, priority 2), (id 6, priority 1), (id 7, priority 1) under FIFO ties.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The order is six, seven, five. Smaller priority wins; arrival puts six before seven. A heap needs the arrival field in its comparator to guarantee this order.

examQuestions.question: Compare n insertions followed by one minimum removal with a stream of alternating insert/remove operations.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An unsorted array makes each insertion constant time and one removal linear, so the first workload costs O(n). Sorting on every insertion can cost O(n squared) total. A binary heap supports both updates in O(log n), which suits mixed workloads. A priority queue ADT does not require the entire array to be sorted.

examQuestions.question: Read job count 0..16 and id/priority integer pairs. Smaller priority is more urgent; ties follow arrival order. Print the prompt and Job: id Priority: priority for each job, using sorted insertion.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>


typedef struct {
    int id;
    int priority;
    int arrival;
} Job;
static int better(Job a, Job b)
{
    return a.priority < b.priority || (a.priority == b.priority && a.arrival < b.arrival);
}
static void insert(Job *items, int *count, Job job)
{
    int i = *count;
    while (i > 0 && better(items[i - 1], job)) {
        items[i] = items[i - 1];
        i--;
    }
    items[i] = job;
    (*count)++;
}

int main(void)
{
    Job items[16];
    int n;
    int count = 0;
    puts("Job count, then id and priority pairs:");
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 0 || n > 16) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        Job job = {.arrival = i};
        if (scanf("%d%d", &job.id, &job.priority) != 2) {
            return 1;
        }
        insert(items, &count, job);
    }
    while (count > 0) {
        Job job = items[--count];
        printf("Job: %d Priority: %d\n", job.id, job.priority);
    }
    return 0;
}
